newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan jobless rate seen steady in '97/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan jobless rate seen steady in '97/98.

text.p: Japan's jobless rate is expected to remain steady or slip slightly in the next business year, economists said in a Reuters poll released on Thursday.
The forecasts from 25 institutions produced a mean average of 3.3 percent for the unemployment rate in 1997/98 from April, a notch below the 3.4 percent forecast for this business year.
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 3.3 percent in November.
The economists said Japan had likely seen the worst of hiring freezes that marked the last two years, and there were few forecasts over 3.4 percent in the quarterly breakdowns.
"We seem to have put the hiring freezes on university graduates behind us," said Junji Ota, an economist at Okasan Economic Research Institute.
The jobless rate, however, is also unlikely to show any substantial easing, economists said.

"There continues to be this mismatch in the labour market -- a gap between the the type of people companies want to employ and the type of jobs people want to do -- which will keep the rate high," said Yasuhiko Ushikubo, an economist at the Industrial Bank of Japan. The survey covered 37 brokerages and research bodies, although not all those polled responded to all the questions.
The survey was conducted between January 13 and 16.
